analysis.one_liner: Makes WIC food benefits a legal guarantee for every eligible low-income mother, infant, and child.
analysis.headline: The bill never got a committee vote and died at the end of the 102nd Congress.
analysis.plain_summary: WIC provides food and nutrition help to low-income pregnant women, new mothers, infants, and young children. Today it is funded year to year, so eligible families can be turned away when money runs out. This bill would have changed the law from 'may' provide benefits to 'shall,' giving every eligible person a legal right to the full benefit and automatically appropriating whatever money is needed.
analysis.who_benefits: Every family that qualifies for WIC — low-income pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under five — would get benefits as a matter of law instead of facing waiting lists or cutoffs when annual funding falls short.
analysis.who_benefits_short: Low-income mothers, infants, and young children

how_it_helps.text: Changes the Child Nutrition Act so the Agriculture Secretary is required, not merely authorized, to run WIC [S3].
States that 'an eligible individual shall be entitled to receive the full amount of benefits authorized,' turning WIC from a discretionary program into an entitlement [S3].
Replaces year-to-year appropriations with permanent funding of 'such sums as may be necessary,' so benefits are not cut off mid-year when money runs out [S3].

analysis.who_pays: Federal taxpayers, who would fund whatever it costs to serve every eligible family as mandatory, open-ended spending rather than a capped annual budget.

drawbacks.text: Making any program an entitlement removes the annual spending cap, so the federal cost is open-ended and no longer weighed against other priorities each year [S3].
Open-ended mandatory spending also removes the ability of future Congresses to adjust program size to economic conditions without changing the underlying law [S3].

analysis.benefit_vs_cost: For the families WIC serves, a legal guarantee of benefits is a large gain — no more being turned away when funding lapses. The honest cost is that Congress gives up annual control over the budget line and commits to paying for every eligible applicant, whatever that costs. That is precisely the trade the bill was about, and Congress never took it up.

outcome.mechanism: It was sent to the Senate Agriculture Committee, then to its nutrition subcommittee, and never got a markup or a vote before the Congress ended.

narrative.text: Sen. DeConcini introduced the bill on February 4, 1992, and it was read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry [S1].
On March 18, 1992, it was referred to the Subcommittee on Nutrition and Investigations [S5].
No further action is recorded; the bill never received a committee markup or a floor vote, and the 102nd Congress ended January 3, 1993 [S5].

outcome.who_came_out_ahead: The bill's death left federal budget control over WIC funding unchanged; no eligible family gained the benefit guarantee it would have provided.

analysis.who_came_out_ahead_short: The status quo: capped annual WIC funding

for.name: Sen. Dennis DeConcini
for.what_they_did: Introduced the bill to make WIC an entitlement.

for.name: Sen. (cosponsor)
for.what_they_did: Signed on as the bill's single cosponsor.

against.name: Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry
against.what_they_did: Held the bill in committee and its nutrition subcommittee without ever scheduling a markup or vote.

sides.party_line_note: The record shows no votes or floor debate, so the partisan shape of any opposition cannot be determined; the bill had one Democratic sponsor and one Democratic cosponsor [S4].

industries.industry: Food retailers and grocers that redeem WIC vouchers
industries.note: WIC benefits are spent on groceries, so a guaranteed, fully funded benefit stream would mean more reliable redemption revenue for stores serving low-income customers.
Formula is a core WIC benefit, so entitling every eligible infant to benefits would lock in and expand the guaranteed market for these products.
